# predictable

> An open-source (MIT) actuarial modelling framework for life insurance cashflow projection.
> A Python authoring DSL compiles to a serialisable, git-diffable computation-graph IR that a Rust
> engine executes. Designed so an LLM can read a Prophet model and reimplement it in predictable
> in minutes, with a machine-readable verification loop: definition-time diagnostics, provenance
> traces, and a structured run-diff against Prophet .rpt output.

Every link below resolves to a file in this repository; a test asserts it. A single fetch of
`llms-full.txt` primes a model with the whole of the normative material.

## Start here

- [IR specification](/docs/design/01-ir.md): the normative format an LLM should write. Shapes, units, timing, expression grammar, builtins. Read this before writing any model.
- [Verification loop](/docs/design/04-verify.md): explain() traces, Prophet readers, run-diff format, tolerance policy, run manifests. Read this before interpreting any diff output.
- [The verification loop end to end](/docs/v2/verification-walkthrough.md): a real four-command rehearsal from "the reserve looks wrong" to one line of `.pir`.
- [Building a model](/docs/v2/building-a-model.md): the DSL from declaration to a checked `.pir`.

## Writing models

- [IR cheatsheet](/skills/predictable-migration/references/ir-cheatsheet.md): shapes, units, timing, grammar and the whole builtin set on one page.
- [IR concepts](/docs/v2/ir-concepts.md) and [.pir syntax](/docs/v2/pir-syntax.md): the data model and the file format.
- [Declaring a model](/docs/v2/dsl-declarations.md) and [the DSL tracer](/docs/v2/dsl-tracer.md): how Python becomes IR.
- [Tables and lookups](/docs/v2/tables.md), [loading modelpoints](/docs/v2/modelpoint-loading.md), [substage levels and terms](/docs/v2/substage-levels.md).
- [Reference models](/docs/v2/reference-models.md): term assurance, monthly term, savings, a solve, IFRS 17 GMM — each one runnable, golden-checked and reconciled.
- [Diagnostics index](/docs/llm/diagnostics.md): every E/W/P/N/H code, its meaning and its fix. Every `doc_url` points here.

## Prophet migration

- [Agent skill](/skills/predictable-migration/SKILL.md): the packaged procedure — inventory, schema first, units and timing as decisions, leaves upward, run and diff, findings top-down, stop condition.
- [The migration loop script](/skills/predictable-migration/scripts/loop.py): check → run → diff → report, one command, JSON out, with the stop condition as booleans.
- [Prophet idiom table](/skills/predictable-migration/references/prophet-idioms.md): Prophet construct → IR construct, including the timing table and the `/12` trap.
- [Migration diagnostics](/skills/predictable-migration/references/diagnostics.md): the codes that actually fire in a migration, and the standard fix for each.
- [Verify-layer formats](/skills/predictable-migration/references/verify-formats.md): `diff.json`, traces and manifests, condensed.
- [Reading Prophet files](/docs/v2/prophet-readers.md): `.MPF`, `.FAC` and `.RPT` readers and their diagnostics.
